title: the Glass Steppe Rising Revisited
premise: When a dying courier presses a scorched map into Felix Kavanagh's hands, the last swordspeaker discovers it points to the Emberhold, where the covenant between the human realms and dragonkind was shattered a decade ago—the same night magic was outlawed and Felix's family was killed. Pursued by the Wardens who enforce the prohibition and shadowed by a runaway Warden apprentice and a charm-hungry street thief, Felix must cross the Glass Steppe to reignite the dragon-fire before it gutters out and the barrier holding back the Hollow Tide collapses. Along the way Felix learns the courier was their presumed-dead sister's ally, and that the covenant was broken not by dragons but by the human chancellors who feared shared power. In the end Felix reforges the covenant at terrible cost—sacrificing their own oath-magic as the final fuel—and chooses a new family over the ghost of the old, returning to the city not as a fugitive but as the first ambassador of a renewed age.
about_author: T. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping steppe grasslands before turning to fantasy. They write stories about inherited debts and the families we build when the old ones burn.

chapters.title: Charms for Copper
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Ten years after the Prohibition, Felix sells luck-knots and fever charms in the smugglers' market of Corrow, invisible and careful. A bleeding courier collapses at their stall, pressing a scorched map into Felix's hands and whispering a name Felix buried with their family. Emotional beat: dread—the past has found them.

chapters.title: The Warden's Knock
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Wardens raid the market hunting the courier's killer; Felix barely escapes with the map, burning their last concealment charm. They learn the courier was a Steppe-runner named Ovid, and the map bears their sister Sera's cipher. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Thief in the Rafters
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A street thief who's been stealing Felix's charms to survive the Warden-camps catches Felix fleeing and blackmails her way into the journey, claiming the map shows the Steppe she was born beside. Emotional beat: wary, transactional alliance with a spark of kinship.

chapters.title: What the Cipher Says
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Decoding Sera's cipher in a safehouse, Felix learns the map leads to the Emberhold and that Sera may have survived the covenant's breaking. A Warden patrol closes in; Felix must choose flight over the city that was her whole careful life. Emotional beat: hope as a dangerous, painful thing.

chapters.title: Out the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The escape from Corrow through the salt gate, aided by an old fence who owes Felix's mother a debt—and betrays their route to the Wardens for pardon. First sight of the Glass Steppe, vast and blinding. Emotional beat: the vertigo of leaving hiding behind.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Who Fell
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Warden apprentice Ilya, ordered to hunt the fugitives, falters when he recognizes the map's seal as his late commander's—and realizes the Wardens' Prohibition hides a massacre. He deserts and follows the trio. Emotional beat: a loyalist's faith cracking.

chapters.title: Glass and Grass
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Crossing the Steppe's glass plains, where fused sand remembers the dragon-fire of the old covenant. Wren teaches Felix steppe-survival; Felix teaches Wren a cantrip, breaking her fear of magic. Emotional beat: found family taking root in hostile ground.

chapters.title: The Hollow Tide
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The party witnesses the Hollow Tide—the devouring emptiness leaking through the failing barrier—swallow a steppe village. Ilya reveals the Wardens know and are evacuating only the capital. Emotional beat: horror, and the moral collapse of the order he served.

chapters.title: Ovid's Letters
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Among Ovid's effects, letters from Sera written after the covenant's breaking: she survived, joined the dragon-loyalists, and sent Ovid to find 'the last speaker' when the Emberhold's fire began to fail. Emotional beat: hope curdling into fear that Sera needs saving, not the world.

chapters.title: The Warden's Net
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wardens corner the party at a steppe waystation; Wren's quick thieving and Ilya's uniform get them through, but Ilya is recognized and branded a traitor. He chooses the fugitives for good. Emotional beat: loyalty declared at a price.

chapters.title: The Dragon-Road
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They find the ancient dragon-road beneath the glass, a tunnel of warm stone where Felix's oath-sword, long dormant, begins to hum. Visions of the covenant's forging: humans and dragons swearing as equals. Emotional beat: awe, and the weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Chancellors Did
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Deeper visions show the truth: the human chancellors broke the covenant themselves, fearing dragon equality, and blamed dragons to justify the Prohibition. Ilya's commander died trying to expose it. Emotional beat: rage at a lie the whole world lives inside.

chapters.title: Wren's Steppe
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The party passes Wren's birth-camp, long destroyed by the Tide; she grieves properly for the first time, and Felix and Ilya stand vigil with her. Emotional beat: mourning shared is mourning halved—the found family solidifies.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. From a high ridge they see the Emberhold's beacon flicker—days from dying. Wardens, now led by Chancellor-Hand Veyne himself, pursue with Tide-lures that drag the Hollow behind them as a weapon. Emotional beat: the clock becomes a countdown.

chapters.title: Veyne's Offer
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Veyne captures Wren and offers Felix a bargain: the map and silence in exchange for Wren's freedom and a pardon—revealing he knows Sera lives and is prisoner in the Emberhold. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, freed by Ilya's diversion, refuses to be leverage and re-joins the others, insisting they storm the Emberhold together. Ilya is gravely wounded holding the pass. Emotional beat: no one is expendable—not anymore.

chapters.title: Storming the Emberhold
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The assault on the Emberhold through Tide-lured storms; Felix's oath-sword fully wakes, cutting a path. They find Sera alive but bound to the failing fire, kept as fuel by Veyne's predecessors. Emotional beat: reunion and horror in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Broken Covenant
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera tells the full truth: the fire fails because it was fed by oath-magic, and the chancellors' lie starved it. Only a freely-given oath can reignite it—and the last oath-bound speaker must give everything. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as both gift and bill.

chapters.title: The Last Oath
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Climax. Veyne unleashes the Hollow Tide into the Emberhold; Felix speaks the reforging covenant, pouring their oath-magic into the fire as Sera, Wren, and wounded Ilya hold the line. The fire roars back, the Tide is sealed, and Veyne is consumed by the lie he served. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into covenant.

chapters.title: Ash and Ember
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The aftermath: Felix survives but magicless, an ordinary sword at their side. Dragons descend to the Emberhold for the first time in a decade; Sera, freed, becomes the Steppe's voice. Emotional beat: exhaustion, tenderness, the strange lightness of survival.

chapters.title: The Ambassador's Road
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The party returns to Corrow, where the Prohibition is crumbling; Felix, as first ambassador, negotiates the city's re-entry into the covenant—using charm-craft, not magic, to win over a frightened council. Emotional beat: the invisible made visible, on their own terms.

chapters.title: A Table Set for Five
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Epilogue. A year later: Felix, Sera, Wren, and recovering Ilya share a small Corrow house; a dragon's shadow crosses the market and no one flinches. Felix plants a luck-knot that grows. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging—the family that chose itself.
